purpose: prospective public-data validation of ODSP state-resolved prediction at previously held-out individuals without reusing closed N2 endpoints

source.dataset_name: MH_ANTWERPEN - Western marsh harriers (Circus aeruginosus) breeding near Antwerp (Belgium)
source.license: public Zenodo archive; reuse subject to archive license

observation_filter.sensor_semantics: GPS events with finite timestamp, coordinates, external temperature and height above mean sea level
observation_filter.temporal_thinning: within each individual, retain the earliest admissible event in each UTC 10-minute bin
observation_filter.reason_no_ground_speed: avoid using an endogenous movement variable as the main ecological/context predictor

prediction_target.semantic_limit: absolute altitude state, not height above ground level

covariates.local_solar_hour_definition: (UTC_decimal_hour + longitude/15) mod 24; equation-of-time correction intentionally omitted
covariates.standardization: for multinomial-logit sensitivity only, center and scale each continuous feature using training-fold moments; zero-SD features fail that sensitivity fold

independence_and_admission.training_individual_weighting: each training individual contributes equal total sample weight regardless of event count
independence_and_admission.heldout_scoring: each held-out individual scored separately; no pooling can rescue a conflicting individual

terminal_rule_primary_rf.generalizing: every eligible held-out individual has mean_log_score_gain > 0
terminal_rule_primary_rf.non_generalizing: every eligible held-out individual has mean_log_score_gain <= 0

claim_ceiling.positive_result_supports: external/context covariates predict absolute altitude-state distributions that transfer across held-out tagged individuals better than a training marginal altitude distribution
does_not_support: height above ground without an independent terrain correction
causal effects of temperature, time or location
removal of GPS or tag measurement bias
universal transferability to other species or regions
